chunks: And with this chain, from Ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Nasr ibn Qabus, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): I asked your father (peace be upon him): Who will be after you? He informed me that you are he. So when Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) passed away, the people went right and left, and I and my companions declared for you. So inform me, who will be after you from your children? He said: My son, so-and-so.

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim, honorific title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, honorific title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: Imamate, the spiritual and political leadership of the Muslims
key_terms.فُلَانٌ: So-and-so, used here to refer to Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam Musa al-Kadhim designate as his successor?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the continuity of the Imamate through the progeny of Imam Musa al-Kadhim, specifically identifying Ali ibn Musa al-Rida as his successor. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (explicit designation), contrasting the firm conviction of Nasr and his companions with the broader confusion (*fitna*) that followed the death of Imam al-Sadiq. This specific chain reinforces the legitimacy of the Ja'fari line and the transition of authority within the Ahl al-Bayt.
